# The Recreational UAS Safety Test

![](https://www.scouting.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/06/trust-logo.png)

Boy Scouts of America© is an [FAA-approved Test Administrator of The
Recreational UAS Safety
Test](https://www.faa.gov/uas/recreational_fliers/knowledge_test_updates/)
(TRUST).

TRUST is a collaboration between the FAA and industry to provide TRUST and
educational safety material to Recreational Flyers.

Recreational flyers can access the [TRUST
here](https://www.faa.gov/uas/recreational_fliers/)

#### Testing Instructions:

  * __

Be sure you are not in an incognito browser

  * __

You must stay within the Exam window throughout your exam

  * __

You must answer all Exam questions. You can not skip exam questions

  * __

Once you have completed the test, remember to print or save a digital copy of
your completion certificate

  * __

When printing the certificate, it should be wallet size

  * __

When emailing the certificate, ensure you are sending it to a valid email
address

  * __

Please access the test through the button below.

[ BEGIN EXAM ](https://faa.scouting.org/FAA/register)

Upon Completion of the test recreational flyers should print or save a digital
copy of their completion certificate and keep it on their person when they
fly. Boy Scouts of America© cannot re-issue your completion certificate if it
is lost. The FAA cannot re-issue your completion certificate. Should you lose
your completion certificate, you will need to re-take TRUST and obtain a new
certificate.

Additional resources:

  * Register your drone through the [FAA Drone Zone](https://faadronezone.faa.gov/#/) before you fly if it weighs more than .55lbs 
  * FAA-Approved UAS Service Suppliers (FAA USSs) of the[ Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability](https://www.faa.gov/uas/programs_partnerships/data_exchange/) (LAANC).
    * LAANC USSs provides FAA approved airspace authorizations and information about airspace restrictions to recreations flyers who wish to fly in controlled airspace 
    * Approved service suppliers have created apps that can be downloaded via apple or google play. Links to the companies are available [here](https://www.faa.gov/uas/programs_partnerships/data_exchange/).
  * [B4UFLY](https://www.faa.gov/uas/recreational_fliers/where_can_i_fly/b4ufly/) provides information about airspace and does not offer airspace authorizations 
  * Information about how to get started as a [recreational flyer](https://www.faa.gov/uas/recreational_fliers/).
